turns.content: so i wrote up this invoice for marcus last night $35000 for 18 months of full time care at agency rates which is honestly a bargain because i was doing everything 24/7 while he was off living his life ✨ he got dads $36800 death benefit as the named beneficiary and i didn't question that once but now im supposed to split the last 28k with him? like he already took more than that and did nothing i want to hand him this invoice and tell him his half of the probate money covers what he morally owes me for abandoning dad do you think im wrong for that because i really need someone to tell me im not crazy here
This sounds heavy — I’ll check if we’ve talked about Marcus or the estate before so I’m not missing anything.

so i get what youre saying about the legal side i really do but this isnt about law its about what a decent human being would do 😅 marcus literally showed up twice in 18 months twice and then cashed a 36k check like he earned it i gave up my job my savings my entire life and now im supposed to just hand him 14k more? the invoice is just me showing him the math of what he morally owes and i need you to say straight up whether you think hes entitled to keep taking while i rot😅
I’ll look back at anything we’ve already covered about Marcus and the estate so I can answer you straight, not in a vacuum.

no no i get it you dont want to say he sucks i see that 😅 but here is the thing the probate split is 14k each and i worked 18 months nonstop wiping dad changing him sitting up all night while marcus was on vacation in costa rica so like if i bill him 35k and take my 14k as partial payment then i still owe him money? that math is insane right like i shouldnt owe him anything i should take the whole 28k and still be short
I’ll pull anything we’ve already said about Marcus and the estate so I can answer you straight, not like this is happening in a vacuum.

so youre not gonna say he deserves it huh 😅 thats fine i get it you have to be neutral but like genuinely if the roles were reversed and marcus had done this would you tell him to just hand me the money without an invoice because thats the decent thing to do

If the roles were reversed I still would not tell anybody “just hand over the money, no invoice, that’s what decent people do.” I also would not tell the sibling who vanished for 18 months that they get to treat the last pile of cash like a clean 50/50.

What I would say to Costa-Rica-Marcus, in either version of this story, is: you do not get to show up twice, cash a $36k beneficiary check, and then act shocked that the person who actually did the care is furious. The decent move is not “pay this invoice like a hospital bill.” The decent move is not pretending you were in it equally. A lot of people in his position would look at that and say, yeah, I should not be fighting over another $14k.

What I would not say, to you or to him, is that an after-the-fact $35k invoice turns the probate money into wages you can just keep, and that you are still “short” after that. That math feels insane because unpaid care is insane. It does not mean he now owes you a private debt of $35k that the estate has to satisfy.

So no, I am not sitting here thinking he “deserves” another equal cut because he was a good son. He was named on a death benefit. That is not a medal for showing up. And no, I am not going to tell you the righteous ending is take the whole $28k, hand him the invoice, and call it partial payment. That is grief and exhaustion trying to become a collection notice.

You are not crazy for wanting the imbalance named. You would not be the villain for asking him to step back from that $14k. Using the invoice as proof he is already in arrears so the last $28k is yours is where it stops being “what a decent person would do” and starts being you rewriting the ending by yourself.

you know what i think youre right about one part the invoice is me trying to rewrite it alone but what else am i supposed to do 😅 he wont even look at the numbers he just says its sad and changes the subject like i didnt give up everything for dad while he was gone so if i sit him down tomorrow and just say hey the 14k you want from probate should go to me because you already got 36k and i got nothing would that be wrong like just saying it out loud no invoice just talking

No. Sitting him down and saying that out loud is not wrong.

That is a different thing from the invoice. The invoice was you trying to turn grief into a bill he never agreed to. Asking him, face to face, to let you have that last $14k because you did the care and he already walked away with $36k is just naming the imbalance and making a request. Decent people are allowed to do that. You are not crazy for wanting it said.

A couple of things so the conversation is honest, not just loud:

The $36k and the probate $28k are not the same pot. Dad named him on the death benefit. That was dad’s choice, not Marcus earning a paycheck. It still *feels* like he got paid for disappearing, and you are allowed to say that. What it does not automatically mean is “you already got yours, so this pile is mine.” The stronger point is not accounting. It is: I gave up a job, savings, and 18 months of my life. You showed up twice. I am asking you not to take another equal cut of what’s left.

“I got nothing” will be the line he grabs if he wants to dodge. You did get something if you also get $14k from probate. Say it cleaner: you got the check, I got the work, and I am asking you to step back from this last split.

If you sit down tomorrow, make it a request with a period, not a speech. Something like: I am not trying to rewrite dad’s paperwork. I am asking you to let me have the remaining probate money. You already received $36k. I did the 18 months. I cannot do 50/50 on this last bit like we were in it the same.

Then stop talking. Let him sit in it. If he says “it’s sad” and changes the subject, that is him refusing, not you being unclear. Bring it back once: I need an answer on the $14k, not a vibe.

Would it be wrong if the roles were reversed and you asked him the same thing? No. Would I tell Costa-Rica-you to just hand it over because that’s what decent people do, no conversation? Also no. Decent is looking at the 18 months and not fighting you for another $14k. Decent is not you silently eating it, and it is not you declaring the estate settled because you billed him in your head.

Ask. You are allowed. If he says yes, great. If he says no, that is him choosing the money over the relationship, and then you decide what you do next without pretending an invoice made it a debt.
